text.p: Headlines from major national newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
EL PAIS
- 80 dead and more than 1,000 injured in full out war between Palestinians and Israelis
- Gonzalez revives polemic by denying that there had been state terrorism
- The budget will create 240,000 jobs and make a big cut in public spending
EL MUNDO
- Palestinian rebellion against Netanyahu disolves into great blood bath
- Gonzalez "If there had been state terrorism the 900 deaths would have been ETA members"
- "That's how relationships are built," said Brunner after receiving the "envelope"; ex-chairman SEAT admits submitting 150 million earned by Aida Alvarez to ambassador
- Social security will cost 175 billion less in this budget
- 30 magistrates in the Supreme Court decide today if they will admit the appeals against the decision not to declassify the CESID papers
DIARIO 16
- Gonzalez unleashes another polemic after denying the state's terrorism
ABC
- "The Tunnel War" explodes: Israelis and Palestinians, in arms
- Positive market reaction to government-CiU agreement to pass the budget
- Aznar meets with Cuevas to reclaim support of the CEOE business association on the pension accord
- General Rodriguez Galindo announces that today there'll be "a very important" statement on his situation
- Violence continues on the streets of the Basque country
CINCO DIAS
- Aznar looks for 100 liberal measures
- Pensions blister up, cause tension among government, unions and businesses
- Telefonica and Unisource lose their French partner
EXPANSION
- Entrecanales and Cubiertas close ranks with a joint foreign subsidiary
- Budget accord injects new energy in the markets
- A British noble joins the court of the Koplowitz sisters
GACETA DE LOS NEGOCIOS
- Public investment accounted for in 1997 budget falls 20 percent
- Ex-chairman SEAT confirms the 150 million payment to Brunner
- PP and CiU accords stimulates buying on the markets
